utterance_understood: The expert rejects treating 'exactly one applicable numeric limit per measurement' as a safe general rule. A measurement may legitimately be compared against zero, one, or several in-force limits when they represent genuinely different requirements (for example daily maximum versus monthly average, or mass versus concentration). Overlapping or staged date intervals are not resolved by picking a winning row; the question is which limit kind the measurement represents. Catalog rows that restate the same requirement should be deduplicated on what the limit actually requires (numeric value, units, and limit kind), not on how many times the row appears. Before counting comparisons, measurements must be matched to the correct limit kind, and superseded limits should drop out even when dates still look plausible.
change_planned: Remove the purpose-A uniqueness requirement that enforced exactly one measurement–limit pair per measurement. Rebuild measurement_limit_pair to include all deduplicated permit-limit rows in force for the permit, outfall, parameter, and monitoring-period interval (not only the limit identifiers carried on the DMR row), while always retaining the DMR-carried limit when present. Add explicit unresolved items for measurement-to-limit-kind matching and for superseded-limit identification, which structured sources alone cannot establish.
remaining_uncertainty: How to match a reported measurement to the correct limit kind (sample type, statistical base, frequency, mass versus concentration) from structured fields alone; which overlapping interval rows are superseded versus concurrently applicable; whether every emitted multi-limit pair should eventually be narrowed before numeric comparison or left as candidate comparisons pending further evidence.
